1.6.literalTaskText: 1.6 S5-b: the expected revision for a commit comes from the journal head; sequence-conflict and duplicate-command refusals proven against races.

currentSourceState.authoritativeCheckIsLegacyOnly: DurableMatchStore.ts:791-806 (verified read) — the ONLY expected-revision check that actually gates a commit reads `mp_match_events` (`MAX(sequence)+1`), inside the SAME transaction as the insert. The journal mirror runs AFTER this transaction commits (mirrorCommittedBatch, called post-tx() at the bottom of appendCommandBatch, verified read) and is explicitly a non-authoritative, best-effort side write ('A mirror failure therefore never fails the command'). So today, 'the expected revision for a commit' comes ENTIRELY from the legacy log; the journal head is never consulted at commit time, only at read time (S2's readEffectiveHead) and recovery time (S4's MatchRecoveryJournalHead).
currentSourceState.existingRaceSafety: The commit-time check IS already race-safe against the legacy log, because it runs inside `this.db.transaction(...)` (better-sqlite3, synchronous, verified read at DurableMatchStore.ts:775). Two overlapping appendCommandBatch calls for the same matchId serialize at the SQLite transaction boundary; the loser sees a genuine revision-conflict or (for a true duplicate commandId) the pre-check at the top of the transaction answers duplicate-command from the stored receipt. This existing safety is legacy-log-scoped, not journal-head-scoped.
currentSourceState.existingTestCoverageIsSplit: matchCommandBatch.test.ts / matchStoreBatchContract.test.ts test the LEGACY revision-conflict/duplicate-command paths. matchStreamJournalMirror.sqlite.test.ts tests the MIRROR's OWN revision-conflict/duplicate-command handling (MatchStreamJournalMirror.ts's kind:'revision-conflict'/'duplicate-command' results), which is a downstream, non-authoritative echo of the SAME journal-side check, not the commit gate. No test exercises the journal head AS the authoritative source for a commit-time decision, because no production code path does that yet.

If the writer ever becomes genuinely async, mirrors for the same match will reorder and the stream will conflict forever.' This is the ONE place a genuine 'race' concern already exists in the codebase for this seam, and it is about the MIRROR's ordering relative to itself across concurrent commits, not about two clients racing a single commit (which the legacy transaction already serializes).

boundedSliceCharter.behavior: Build a MODE-GATED (test-override only, never touching the 'off' default) alternate expected-revision resolution path modeled directly on S4's MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts pattern (same 'legacy | journal | diverged'-shaped tri-state, but for the WRITE/commit side instead of the recovery side), and a race-proof test suite that drives concurrent appendCommandBatch calls against a real SQLite-backed match store with the journal mirror active under `_setCombatJournalAuthorityModeForTests('shadow'|'enabled')`, proving: (a) two commits racing the SAME expectedRevision — exactly one wins with a typed sequence/revision-conflict for the loser; (b) two commits with the SAME commandId (a genuine duplicate, e.g. a retried client) resolve to the IDENTICAL receipt regardless of arrival order; (c) the mirror's OWN revision-conflict/duplicate-command arms (already implemented in MatchStreamJournalMirror.ts, currently untested per S1 review RR-5 for two of its arms) are exercised by the SAME race, not just by hand-constructed unit inputs.
boundedSliceCharter.raceRealismCaveat: better-sqlite3 executes transactions synchronously on the Node main thread; a 'race' cannot be a true OS-level race without literally forking processes or using worker_threads against the same SQLite file. The realistic, valuable race to prove is at the ASYNC BOUNDARY the codebase actually has: `tx()` (sync, legacy-authoritative) followed by `await this.mirrorCommittedBatch(...)` (async, non-authoritative) — i.e., two `appendCommandBatch` calls fired without awaiting the first, exercising Node's microtask interleaving between the synchronous transaction commits and their asynchronous mirror follow-ups. This is precisely RR-2's concern. Recommend the slice's 'race' claim be scoped honestly to this interleaving, not oversold as a multi-process concurrency proof.

State this as a recommendation requiring owner sign-off on the exact timeout value, not a unilateral implementation choice.

RR-4: the single-vs-two-writer architecture. RECOMMENDATION: given how much analogous machinery ALREADY exists on the campaign side (appendCampaignCommandBatch's atomic-batch-plus-verify-after-apply pattern), recommend the owner decide whether combat should eventually adopt the SAME pattern (journal as sole write authority; mp_match_events becomes a derived/replay-only projection) as a LATER change, OR whether S7-d should instead formally document the two-writer reconciliation story (mirror failure -> shadow-mismatch counter -> S4's divergence refusal -> match blocked pending operator repair) AS the permanent answer to RR-4's SHALL tension, accepting that 'the authoritative transaction' in spec language maps to 'the match-file transaction, with the journal as an eventually-consistent, refusal-gated mirror' rather than literally one transaction.
